explain.say: In 1602 the Dutch East India Company sold shares to the public in Amsterdam, and people began trading them on what became the world's first modern stock exchange. A grocer could own a sliver of a fleet sailing to Asia. Look at the timeline of capitalism, from merchants to factories to global finance.

explain.say: What is capitalism? Watch the cycle. Private owners invest capital, money used to make more money. They pay wages and buy machines, make goods, sell them in competitive markets, and reinvest the profit. Round and round, it grows, and sometimes crashes. Which step depends most on people choosing to buy?

stages.ask: What is capitalism and when did it begin?

explain.say: Now two great thinkers. Adam Smith in 1776 praised the division of labour and said markets guide self-interest, as if by an invisible hand. Karl Marx in 1867 argued profit came from workers' unpaid labour and that crises were built in. Later, Max Weber linked capitalism to religious culture, and Karl Polanyi said society pushes back against markets. Whose view convinces you more?

draw.name: x-compare
draw.verdict: Weber, Polanyi and others added culture and society.

explain.say: Here are real numbers from Angus Maddison: average world output per person, in 1990 dollars. About 667 in 1820, about 1,500 by 1913, about 6,500 by 2003, nearly ten times higher. Yet growth was very unequal between countries and classes. What changes when a society grows ten times richer?

items.ask: How much richer has the world become?

explain.say: Look at the map. Capitalism took many forms: Dutch trade, British industry, American corporations, Japanese and German coordinated firms, and China's state-led markets. Sven Beckert shows early cotton capitalism rested on slavery and conquest. Great work. Exam tip: say which capitalism, where and when.

faq.q: What is capitalism and when did it begin?
faq.a: An economic system in which private owners invest capital, hire wage labour and produce goods for profit in competitive markets. Historians date its origins variously to medieval Italian and Dutch merchants, to agrarian England, or to the Industrial Revolution.

faq.q: What is the difference between Smith and Marx?
faq.a: Adam Smith, in The Wealth of Nations, 1776, argued that the division of labour and competitive markets increase wealth. Karl Marx, in Capital, 1867, argued that capitalists profit from workers' unpaid labour, that crises are built in, and that the system would be overthrown.
asks: What did Marx mean by surplus value?

faq.q: How much richer has the world become?
faq.a: By Angus Maddison's estimates, average world GDP per person rose from about 667 dollars in 1820 to about 6,516 in 2003, in 1990 dollars: nearly ten times. The gains were very unevenly shared between and within countries.

faq.q: What was the Dutch East India Company?
faq.a: The VOC, founded in 1602, was a trading company with government powers in Asia. It sold shares to the public, traded on the Amsterdam exchange, and used armed force, including conquest and enslaved labour, in the spice trade.
asks: What was the first stock exchange?

faq.a: A theory by Peter Hall and David Soskice, 2001, contrasting liberal market economies like the USA and Britain with coordinated market economies like Germany and Japan, where firms, unions and banks cooperate more closely.

facts: The Dutch East India Company was founded in 1602.
Adam Smith's The Wealth of Nations was published in 1776.
The first volume of Marx's Capital appeared in 1867.

quiz.say: World output per person rose from about 667 to about 6,516 dollars. About how many times higher is that?
quiz.why: 6,516 divided by 667 is about 9.8, close to ten.

quiz.say: Which thinker argued that crises are built into capitalism?
quiz.show: Built-in crises were a key argument of…
quiz.why: Marx argued that competition and falling profits lead to repeated crises.

wrong.1: Smith argued markets usually increase wealth.
wrong.2: Maddison was an economic historian who measured growth.
